ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 regulations and MFAT sanctions lists, US OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdictions. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified and subjected to enhanced due diligence under Part 2 of the AML/CFT Act 2009, including source of funds and source of wealth verification, senior management approval, and ongoing monitoring. Adverse media screening and risk-based transaction monitoring must be implemented per the reporting entity's AML/CFT programme.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Registration Portal (part of the Companies Register at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Māori; may include Māori words, but all characters must be in the Latin alphabet. Names cannot exceed 100 characters. Non-English script (e.g., Chinese characters) is not permitted. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless an exemption is granted under s.25 Companies Act 1993. Words implying a connection to the Crown, government, or regulated professions require consent. Name availability is determined by identity with existing names; similar names may be rejected if confusion is likely.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies under s.26 Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days of the rejection notice, providing grounds and evidence of consent or distinctiveness. The Registrar must make a decision on the appeal; if the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review. No extension of the 30-day reservation is available except that the name reservation is automatically extended during an active incorporation process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are generally permissible for registered office compliance in New Zealand for a private company, provided the service provider has a physical street address in New Zealand and accepts service of legal process on behalf of the company. However, for a deep-sea Ro-Ro vessel shipping operation claiming New Zealand tax residence or treaty benefits, the company must demonstrate real commercial substance beyond virtual office, including local board meetings, operational management, decision-making, and vessel chartering activities conducted from New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% probability per annum for a standard private international shipping company; higher (65%) if the company claims tax residence benefits or is selected for AML/CFT supervision by the DIA/FMA or is on the Companies Office compliance inspection trigger list.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) — ss 9–12 (Incorporation Procedure), s 13 (Certificate of Incorporation), ss 31–33 (Constitution), ss 122–125 (Appointment of Directors and Officers), s 189 (Registered Office), s 198D (Filing Requirements), and ss 201–208 (Share Capital and Calls)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Te Ahumairangi), a business function of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (Hīkina Whakatutuki), 4-8 Whitmore Street, Wellington 6140, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 — Company Incorporation Application under Regulation 6 of the Companies Act 1993 Form Regulations, filed via the New Zealand Companies Office Online Register (NZRN) with simultaneous issuance of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital for international companies. Shares may be issued for nil, par, or nominal consideration as recorded in the share register. There is no statutory escrow account requirement under the Companies Act 1993. The company must, however, maintain an accurate share register under s 87 and ensure that any consideration for issued shares is received and evidenced in board minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMPANY REFERRED TO HEREIN. Pursuant to the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) and the Constitution of the Company, the undersigned duly appointed founding directors adopt the following unanimous resolutions: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the subscriptions of the founding shareholders for the Class A Ordinary Shares set forth in the Register of Shares be and are hereby accepted; that the shares be issued fully paid as fully paid shares, and that the consideration for such shares be credited to the share capital account of the company in accordance with s 201 of the Companies Act 1993, with any premium credited to the share premium account; (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the company in New Zealand be and is hereby established at [Full Street Address, City, Postal Code, New Zealand], and that an application be irrevocably forwarded to the Registrar of Companies for registration of such address pursuant to s 189 of the Companies Act 1993; (3) APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [Name A] be and is hereby appointed Sole Director and Chief Executive Officer of the company; that [Name B] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer (where applicable); and that such officers are severally authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts with registered banks in New Zealand for the purposes of SWIFT letter-of-credit and wire-transfer payment rails; (4) BUSINESS AUTHORISATION: RESOLVED that the officers be and are hereby authorized to execute, under customary corporate formalities, all charterparty agreements, bill-of-lading contracts, terminal access agreements, and all statutory filings required for the conduct of deep-sea roll-on/roll-off (Ro-Ro) vessel vehicle transport under ISIC 5012, including the Maritime New Zealand operator licence application; and (5) REGULATORY FILING: RESOLVED that the board do hereby authorize the preparation and filing of the incorporation instrumentation with the New Zealand Companies Office and the application to Inland Revenue for an IRD income tax and GST registration certificate, and that any director or secretary be authorized to sign and lodge such documents. RESOLVED FURTHER that the model constitution as set out in s 122 of the Companies Act 1993 be adopted until otherwise amended by special resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and NZBN Pre-incorporation Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Online Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for reservation of the proposed company name in accordance with ss 22–24 of the Companies Act 1993. The name must not be identical or nearly identical to an existing registered name or a restricted name such as 'Bank', 'Trust', or 'Vessel' as appropriate. Simultaneously the system checks for availability of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and the legality of the name against prohibited offensive/relevant terms. Once reserved, the name is held for a statutory period of 20 working days within which the incorporation application must be filed.
required_dossiers: Consent to use and standard form notice if a restricted term is included
Physical postal address for correspondence in New Zealand
Name and tax identification details of the ultimate beneficial owner (BOI) for the Companies Office beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a fresh application with alternative names; if the rejection arises from a misleading/offensive ground, the applicant may seek a review under s 24 of the Companies Act 1993 within 20 working days, or apply to the District Court for a declaratory judgment on the registerability of the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitution and Shareholders' Subscription Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Solicitor or Authorised Incorporation Agent retained by the founding shareholders (governed by Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders and the first director(s) must execute the company constitution, which must comply with ss 31–33 of the Companies Act 1993. If a custom constitution is used, it must set out the share classes, voting rights, director appointment rules, and distribution provisions. The share subscription agreement must identify the number of shares, the consideration per share, and any reserves. Where the entity is tax-exempt by policy, the constitution should restrict share transfers to maintain non-resident ownership. All documents must be dated and executed with Chinese or English witnesses as applicable to overseas signatories.
required_dossiers: Signed constitution (adopting model or custom form)
Consent of directors to act in writing (s 123)
Certified passport copies of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
BN/BOI declaration form for the beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the constitution is defective or fails the filing validation, the incorporation agent will amend and re-execute the document electronically; if any director is bereaved of capacity, a substituted director must be appointed by separate shareholder resolution prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Online Register portal) / MBIE Registry Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the NZ Companies Office portal, execute Form 2 (Company Incorporation Application), and lodge the constitution and the certificates for directors and shareholders. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 105.41 (including GST) via debit/credit card or client payment portal. The application will be algorithmically validated and, where the entity is an international shipping company, the officer will tag the industry code ISIC 5012. The register will automatically reserve the NZBN and generate the provisional company number.
required_dossiers: Form 2 complete with company name, registered office address, and postal address
Certificate of incorporation application fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a notice of query or 'request for further information' pursuant to s 360 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant has strict time limits to respond; the incorporation agent will file the supplementary declaration and, if the query arises from a technical fault, an updated Form 2 may be re-submitted. A rejected application does not result in the loss of the name if a re-application is filed within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN Issuance, and Filing of Initial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful validation, the Registrar issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation under s 13 of the Companies Act 1993, and the NZBN is displayed on the register certificate. The company must thereafter lodge a register of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners within 10 working days. The registered office and principal place of business must be entered on the public register, and a registered address for service must be verified for valid delivery of civil documents together with any—entity maps for the Shipping Act liability framework—the officer will obtain the certified copy of the certificate for bank due diligence.
required_dossiers: Register of Shareholders including initial allotment details
Beneficial ownership register (available for inspection by regulated authorities)
Consent to act of directors for company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated or the register displays erroneous shareholdings, the officer may apply under s 161 of the Companies Act 1993 for a correction to the register, or under s 360 for a rectification of any administrative error by the Registrar, supported by an affidavit from the incorporator.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online portal myIR available at ird.govt.nz. The New Zealand Companies Office administers the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and company registration, which is a prerequisite for most tax registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or international shipping company with a New Zealand taxable presence must first obtain an NZBN from the Companies Office. The entity must then request an IRD number using the prescribed IR596 form or through the myIR online service, supported by certified constitutional documents, proof of address, and evidence of the foreign entity's existence. For GST purposes, registration is mandatory if annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000; a non-resident may also apply for voluntary GST registration to claim input credits or to zero-rate exported shipping services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' system. Eligible close companies may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status to achieve tax transparency, subject to the Income Tax Act 2007. Hybrid mismatch provisions under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 may deny deductions or require inclusion for certain cross-border hybrid arrangements. International shipping entities should also examine the specific statutory concessions and foreign-sourced income exemption rules applicable to non-resident operators of overseas vessels.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 per 12-month period of taxable supplies in New Zealand; voluntary registration is available for non-resident businesses, including international shipping operators supplying zero-rated export or transport services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. E-invoicing operates on a voluntary Peppol-compliant framework. GST returns must be filed electronically via myIR, with filing frequencies depending on turnover. Shipment-level customs data is declared electronically through the New Zealand Customs Service trade single window (CUSDEC).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for supplies of goods physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply. Services supplied to a non-resident outside New Zealand may be zero-rated when the services are received and consumed outside New Zealand. International transport services, including sea freight and ancillary shipping services related to Ro-Ro vehicle carriage, are zero-rated where the destination is outside New Zealand. Appropriate contemporaneous evidence must be retained to substantiate the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (through or direct non-negotiable)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank foreign-exchange confirmation
Vessel/sailing schedule or port loading evidence
Charter party or booking confirmation for Ro-Ro cargo
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD and the New Zealand Customs Service may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. In the absence of compliant export documentation, the supply is treated as taxable at 15% GST, and the zero-rating may be retrospectively clawed back with interest. Civil shortfall penalties ranging from 20% to 150% of the evaded tax may apply depending on culpability, with the maximum 150% penalty for fraudulent evasion. Criminal prosecution may lead to fines of up to NZD 50,000 or imprisonment. Recovery and garnishment powers are available under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the central bank and prudential regulator for all banks operating in New Zealand and for the New Zealand dollar (NZD), which circulates throughout the Realm of New Zealand, including the Cook Islands where the International Company (CK_IC) is incorporated. The Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission regulates licensed financial services providers in the Cook Islands, while cross-border banking, FX, and clearing rails for this structure clear through RBNZ-regulated New Zealand banks using the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) RTGS platform.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The NZD is a fully convertible hard currency under IMF Article VIII obligations. New Zealand maintains an open capital account and a fully liberalised current account; there are no exchange control permits, conversion quotas, or profit-remittance authorisations. Non-resident shareholders of the Ro-Ro carrier International Company may receive dividends, loan repayments, charter-hire receipts, and liquidation proceeds in NZD or any deliverable foreign currency without FX regulatory approval. The only remittance hurdles are fiscal: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at the statutory rate of 15%, reducible to 5% for dividends under the NZ–China Double Tax Agreement where treaty eligibility is met, or to applicable rates under other DTA jurisdictions; and, for a non-resident International Company deriving no New Zealand-sourced domestic shipping income, no New Zealand income tax exposure is anticipated. Practical convertibility constraints arise solely from bank-side AML/CFT source-of-funds verification and economic-substance due diligence, not from statute or central bank decree.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable under New Zealand law. The Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1984, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 imposes no surrender, repatriation, or mandated conversion ratio for export proceeds. Freight and charter-hire revenue generated by the Deep-Sea Ro-Ro carrier may be retained indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts either onshore in New Zealand or offshore without conversion to NZD. Settlement banks must record an IMF BPM6 Balance-of-Payments purpose code (e.g., 'SA540 – Transport / Freight' or 'C340 – Charter hire') for statistical reporting and cross-border monitoring, but no statutory timeline applies to surrender or repatriation, and no ratio of export proceeds must be converted into local currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (multi-currency: NZD, USD, EUR, AUD, JPY, GBP)
Operational Account with dedicated FX hedging line and Trade Finance / Commercial LC desk
Operational Account and specialised Shipping, Trade and Commodity Finance Account
Operational Account (NZD/FCY) — viable once an enhanced remote KYC interview and economic-substance file are approved
Operational Account — generally limited to domestic retail/SME profile; less suitable for an offshore International Company in Ro-Ro shipping

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. New Zealand has no dedicated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence class; non-bank payment providers must instead register as financial service providers under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2011 and comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 as supervised by the Department of Internal Affairs. Offshore EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Wise, Currencycloud, MultiPass) may be used as complementary collection and FX-conversion wallets for sub-threshold operational disbursements, but they are not licensed to take deposits from the New Zealand public, cannot issue commercial letters of credit, and cannot provide committed treasury hedging lines. The primary settlement accounts, SWIFT rails, and trade-finance infrastructure must reside with RBNZ-registered banks; EMI rails are permissible only for ancillary expense payments and must not become the sole conduit for inbound equity capital or outbound charter-hire settlements due to bank chain-of-custody and sanctions-screening concerns.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate exists for directors of an offshore International Company to appear physically in New Zealand. RBNZ-regulated banks permit remote account opening where the company passes enhanced due diligence, using (1) a recorded video interview of at least one director or authorised signatory, (2) electronic identity verification of beneficial owners, and (3) apostilled or certified corporate documents, including the Certificate of Incorporation, Register of Directors, Register of Beneficial Owners, and Memorandum/Articles. Physical in-branch attendance is not universally required but may be triggered by the bank's risk appetite where the structure involves discretionary trusts, nominee shareholders, or high-risk trade corridors. For the stated Low_Risk_Standard AML tier of the Ro-Ro carrier, a virtual interview is acceptable provided the statutory shipping licence evidence and economic-substance documentation are supplied concurrently. Remote onboarding is expressly permitted under the AML/CFT Act 2009 using electronic identity verification and secure video conferencing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership — International Company shares held through nominee shareholders or a discretionary trust in the Cook Islands.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) notarised Register of Beneficial Owners identifying all natural persons with a controlling interest or exercise of ultimate control; (2) trust deed or settlement excerpt and trustee resolution demonstrating beneficial entitlement; (3) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations for each beneficial owner; (4) certified extract from the Cook Islands Registrar of International Companies confirming valid incorporation and good standing; (5) ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC entity-mapping sheet reconciling the International Company structure with the New Zealand banking counterparty; (6) digital identity verification results for each director and authorised signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance deficiency — an offshore International Company with no physical nexus to New Zealand or demonstrable vessel-operating substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) binding BIMCO Ro-Ro charter party agreements linking the International Company to principal charterers; (2) vessel AIS voyage log and port-call schedule substantiating the Deep-Sea Ro-Ro route; (3) New Zealand agent-appointment letter under ISIC 5012 / NAICS 483111; (4) contracts for tug, pilot, stevedoring, bunker, and terminal services paid from the International Company's operating account; (5) tax residence certificates of each beneficial owner; (6) registered-office and physical-presence evidence in the Cook Islands or New Zealand as applicable; (7) board minutes containing a commercial-rationale narrative consistent with the Company's purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or invalid statutory maritime licence, ship registration, or P&I insurance — a hard blocker because the business scope expressly requires a statutory licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) Maritime New Zealand operating licence or equivalent flag-state safety certificate issued under the Maritime Transport Act 1994; (2) ship registration certificate under the Ship Registration Act 1992 or the relevant flag-state registry; (3) P&I Club Blue Card and Certificate of Entry; (4) ISM (International Safety Management) Code certificate and ISPS (International Ship and Port Facility Security) certificate; (5) pollution-response plan and Certificate of Financial Responsibility; (6) hull and machinery insurance cover note with loss-payable clauses to any mortgagee bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or high-risk trade corridor — Ro-Ro routes touching ports in jurisdictions subject to New Zealand or United Nations sanctions (New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) written sanctions-compliance narrative confirming screening of every charterer, shipper, consignee, cargo owner, and vessel; (2) UNSC, OFAC, and New Zealand sanctions screening output for all counterparties; (3) cargo manifests and bills of lading mapping each voyage to permissible cargo categories (e.g., vehicles, rolling stock, heavy machinery); (4) beneficial-ownership and politically-exposed-person screening results for all directors and BOs; (5) trade-based money-laundering controls evidencing congruence between freight invoices, AIS positions, and port-call bills; (6) annual negative-screening sign-off by the appointed compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity capital injections from the ultimate parent or shareholder via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV into the International Company's NZD or USD settlement account held at ANZ, BNZ, or Westpac. On every incoming wire, include the IMF BPM6 Balance-of-Payments purpose code for foreign direct investment (A1200 – Equity capital) and a payment narrative reading 'FDI – share capital subscription – International Company CK_IC – ISIC 5012 Deep-Sea Ro-Ro carrier'. Provide the receiving bank with a board resolution authorising the share allotment, an updated shareholder register, and a source-of-funds statement from the remitting entity. Where the inward injection exceeds NZD 10 million within a rolling 12-month period, or would confer control over significant business assets or sensitive land, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent analysis must be completed; a mere capital injection into a non-resident International Company for vessel operating capital ordinarily does not require OIA consent, but the bank will request written confirmation. No RBNZ approval, exchange-control permit, or conversion obligation applies; the injected capital may remain in USD, EUR, or AUD indefinitely.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clear operational and trade settlements through RBNZ-regulated banks using the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 with gpi (Global Payments Innovation) tracking for bunker fuel, port dues, canal tolls, crew wages, and agency fees; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 for vessel acquisition, dry-dock repairs, and import of specialised Ro-Ro loading equipment; (3) Documentary Collections governed by URC 522 for freight and charter-hire receivables; (4) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank reimbursements supporting LC confirmations; (5) ESAS RTGS and Payment Systems Coordination Group rails for NZD domestic clearing legs; and (6) CLS settlement for NZD foreign-exchange legs to eliminate settlement risk. Each disbursement must carry the corresponding BOP purpose code (e.g., SA540 – freight transport services, C340 – charter hire) and be supported by invoices, port receipts, liquidation statements, or LC documentation retained for compliance audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (NZD vs USD, EUR, AUD, JPY, GBP) — the standard hedge for freight revenue and bunker-cost currency exposure
FX Swaps (rolling deliverable swaps) for managing short-term liquidity mismatches between receipt and disbursement currencies
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for tenor-matched hedging of USD-denominated finance leases against NZD or EUR-denominated charter revenue
European-style FX Options and FX Collars for targeted freight-rate and currency scenarios, with premium-paying or costless-collar structures executed under bank credit lines
CLS-settled Spot FX Transactions for same-day conversion with settlement-risk elimination; NZD is a CLS-eligible, fully deliverable currency

Not Permissible in Practice: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) and NDF options for NZD, because the NZD is fully convertible and deliverable onshore; RBNZ-regulated banks execute deliverable forwards instead, and any attempted synthetic NDF would be recharacterised as a deliverable forward for prudential and reporting purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Company Annual Return) - Companies Act 1993, s.208
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of incorporation or on the alternate filing date approved by the Registrar; the filing date may be changed once in any 12-month period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of NZ$150 per unpaid annual-return fee; the Registrar may strike the company off the Register after notice if the annual-return fee remains unpaid for two months and the return is unfiled for two consecutive years; restoration is available only by court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and auditor's report - Financial Reporting Act 2013, s.35 (for large or FMC-reporting entities only)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the balance date (e.g., 31 August for a 31 March balance date); small non-reporting companies are exempt from filing financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringement fine up to NZ$10,000 and a NZ$100-per-day daily penalty per defaulting director; persistent non-filing may instigate strike-off proceedings and personal liability for directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4) - Income Tax Act 2007
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 7 months after the balance date (31 October for a standard 31 March balance date); the return deadline may be aligned with an approved non-standard balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZ$250 for remote filing; incremental late-filing penalties and use-of-money interest apply to unpaid provisional and terminal tax; serious non-compliance can lead to IRD prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Beneficial-Ownership CDD Record and annual internal compliance assurance note - AML/CFT Act 2009
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT Supervisor) - maintained on site for inspection rather than lodged as a public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Refreshed upon any material change of beneficial ownership and at least once every 12 months; shareholder allotments must be notified to the Registrar within 15 working days and changes of directors within 20 working days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML/CFT Act 2009 civil penalties up to NZ$200,000 for a body corporate and NZ$2,000 per day for continuing failures, with director liability exposure

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is imposed under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for (i) FMC reporting entities and (ii) large companies, defined as those exceeding total assets of NZ$60 million or total revenue of NZ$30 million in each of the two immediately preceding consecutive accounting periods. A shareholder holding at least 5% of the voting rights may also requisition an audit of any size company. Small non-listed, non-reporting companies are exempt from audit unless requisitioned.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP): Tier 1 and Tier 2 for-profit entities apply NZ IFRS (full or reduced disclosure regime); Tier 3 and Tier 4 apply simplified NZ GAAP standards for small non-complex entities; financial statements must be expressed in New Zealand dollars unless functional-currency relief is approved under NZ IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a public UBO register. The annual return to the Registrar of Companies confirms current shareholder and director particulars and constitutes the annual statutory declaration of ownership. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the company's share register and reflected in the next annual return at the anniversary date. Separately, under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the company's registered agent or company secretary, acting as a reporting entity, must conduct ongoing customer due diligence on every ultimate beneficial owner, refresh the CDD record upon any material change of control of 5% or more, and at least once every 12 months. Director appointments and resignations must be notified to the Companies Office within 20 working days, and share allotments within 15 working days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–1,500 per annum for a licensed New Zealand registered-office and company-secretarial agent (includes annual-return preparation, statutory register custody, registered address and mail handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000–45,000 per annual statutory audit for a medium-size deep-sea Ro-Ro shipowning or operating entity when the audit is compulsory; USD 3,000–8,000 where a compilation or review report suffices under small-company exemptions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand resident companies are taxed at 28% on worldwide income. A Cook Islands International Company (IC) registered under the International Companies Act 2003 is tax-exempt in the Cook Islands on foreign-sourced income and, if its central management and control (CMC) is not in New Zealand, is treated as a non-resident for New Zealand tax, thereby avoiding New Zealand corporate income tax on non-New Zealand-sourced shipping income. For a foreign-flag Ro-Ro vessel engaged in international voyages, the New Zealand foreign-shipping exemption under section FH 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007 may exempt profits from international freight and charter hire from New Zealand tax, provided the vessel does not carry coastal New Zealand cargo. No statutory tax holiday applies to a New Zealand resident shipping company other than the general 28% rate, though eligible R&D expenditure may attract a 150% deduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via myIR, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) online portal; non-resident companies with New Zealand-sourced income use IR4NZ or IR4 with the non-resident section, also filed through myIR or a registered tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the end of the tax year, unless a tax agent with a valid extension has been appointed. For non-standard balance dates, the return is due on the 7th day of the seventh month after the balance date, or as advised by IRD. Any terminal tax for non-provisional taxpayers is due by 7 April following the income year, and provisional tax is payable in three installments (28 August, 15 January, and 7 May for a standard balance date).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and IRD number; confirm legal entity name as registered in Cook Islands or New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name of the IC and obtain an IRD number via non-resident company registration if the IC has any New Zealand-source income or a New Zealand-sourced withholding tax obligation. If no New Zealand tax nexus exists, no return is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Type of company and tax residency status; select 'Non-resident company' if CMC is not in New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate non-resident status if the IC's board meetings and strategic decisions occur in the Cook Islands or another non-New Zealand jurisdiction. Be aware of de facto CMC tests using actual management location.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income derived from New Zealand sources, including gross freight, charter hire, demurrage, or deadfreight from voyages loading or unloading in New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-source income. International Ro-Ro voyages are generally sourced offshore if both loading and discharge are outside New Zealand; if a voyage calls at a New Zealand port, allocate income using voyage apportionment consistent with New Zealand's source rules and any applicable DTA shipping article.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses incurred in deriving the income reported in Box 6, including fuel, port charges, crew wages, charter hire, vessel depreciation, insurance, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim expenses only to the extent attributable to New Zealand-source income. For a non-resident IC, expenses must be apportioned on a reasonable basis. If the IC has no New Zealand PE, the foreign-shipping exemption removes income and therefore no expenses are deducted. If a PE exists, allocate profits under the OECD authorised OECD approach and apply transfer pricing rules to related-party expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (or loss) after deducting allowable expenses and offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income as New Zealand-source income minus allocated expenses. Tax losses may be carried forward only if the 49% continuity of ownership test is satisfied; non-resident ICs must file the appropriate loss continuity election and ownership schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) details for resident companies; non-resident companies generally do not complete this box unless they hold an ICA as a resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC is not required to maintain an ICA. If the IC is treated as a New Zealand resident for tax, dividends paid must be fully imputed to reduce the residual withholding tax rate from 30% to 15% (subject to treaty reduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable calculation: taxable income multiplied by 28%, less tax credits such as foreign tax credits, RWT, and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign-shipping exemption applies, tax payable is nil. If tax applies, claim foreign tax credits for Cook Islands or flag-state income taxes paid under New Zealand's ordinary credit rules or DTA provisions. No DTA credit exists for Cook Islands tax on dividends from an IC if not actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signatures, plus disclosure of any related-party transactions or transfer pricing positions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC's local representative or director must sign the return. Attach any transfer pricing disclosure schedules (IR1073) if the IC has cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZ$10 million, and include a statement that the IC is tax resident in the Cook Islands and not in New Zealand, with supporting board meeting minutes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of an IR4 return attracts a late filing penalty of NZ$250, with an additional NZ$50 per month for each month the return is outstanding, up to a maximum of NZ$1,000. Late payment of tax incurs an initial late payment penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax plus an additional 1% per month thereafter. Use-of-money interest (UOMI) applies on underpayments at the prescribed IRD rate, currently 8.92% per annum for underpayments as of 2025. For non-resident companies, penalties apply only if a filing obligation exists; failure to file a nil return with no New Zealand-source income may still attract a penalty if the IRD has issued a demand.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory NRWT on dividends paid by a New Zealand resident company to a non-resident recipient is 15% where the dividend is fully imputed, and 30% where not imputed. For a Cook Islands IC that has no New Zealand tax residency and derives only foreign-source income, dividends paid to its shareholders are not subject to New Zealand NRWT because the dividend is not sourced in New Zealand. However, if the IC is managed and controlled in New Zealand and thus a New Zealand tax resident, dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to NRWT at 15% or 30% unless a reduced treaty rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a dividend is paid by a New Zealand resident company to a Cook Islands resident shareholder, the recipient must submit a valid Cook Islands tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, along with an approved NRWT rate application form (IR372) and a declaration of beneficial ownership. The withholding agent (the company) must withhold NRWT at the statutory rate unless the IRD has approved a reduced treaty rate. The New Zealand–Cook Islands DTA provides for a maximum dividend withholding rate of 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of the voting power, and 15% in other cases. For shipping enterprises, the DTA's shipping article exempts international shipping profits from New Zealand tax, and the protocol also prevents double taxation of income taxable in the Cook Islands. The TRC is valid for the relevant income year and must be renewed annually. Failure to hold a valid TRC or to file the rate application before payment results in the statutory rate applying.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest paid by a New Zealand resident to a non-resident is 15%, reducible to 2% under the approved issuer levy (AIL) regime if certain conditions are met (non-resident lender, no associated New Zealand issuer, and interest paid on a registered security). Statutory NRWT on royalties paid to a non-resident is 15%. Under the New Zealand–Cook Islands DTA, interest is taxed at a maximum of 10% in the source state, and royalties at a maximum of 5% (or 10% for some literary royalties). For cross-border shipping leases or bareboat charters, payments may be characterised as royalties or industrial royalties only if they are for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment, and treaty rates may apply. The IC must document the beneficial ownership of each payment and obtain IRD determination where a reduced rate is claimed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand's transfer pricing documentation rules require contemporaneous Master File and Local File documentation where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZ$10 million in an income year. The Local File must include entity overview, controlled transactions, functional analysis, and an arm's-length analysis using the most appropriate methodology. The Master File is required for multinational groups with total consolidated group revenue above NZ$1 billion and transactions with a New Zealand entity exceeding NZ$10 million. Simplified documentation is available for low-risk distributors and service providers meeting specific thresholds. Even below the threshold, documentation should be kept if the arrangement carries significant transfer pricing risk, as the IRD may issue a notice requiring documentation. Penalties apply for failure to keep or provide documentation: 20% of the resulting tax shortfall, increased to 40% if the taxpayer did not take reasonable care or the shortfall is attributable to transfer pricing manipulation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Cook Islands IC regime does not have a codified Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the Cayman Islands or BVI. However, the Cook Islands International Companies Act 2003 requires that the IC maintains a registered office in the Cook Islands, a licensed registered agent, and a register of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners. A lack of physical presence, commercial substance, and actual decision-making in the Cook Islands is a critical risk factor under New Zealand tax law. Under the CMC doctrine, if the actual senior management of the Ro-Ro shipping business exercises direction and control from New Zealand, the IC is deemed a New Zealand tax resident and taxed on worldwide income at 28%. New Zealand's general anti-avoidance rule (section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007) and the CFC rules may also apply to reattribute income to New Zealand shareholders or to strike down arrangements lacking commercial reality. For a deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle carrier, economic substance is evidenced by owning or chartering the vessel, employing the crew, maintaining technical management, negotiating charter parties, and exercising commercial oversight outside New Zealand. The IC must maintain contemporaneous records demonstrating that board meetings, bank accounts, and management functions are genuinely performed in the Cook Islands or a recognised offshore jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to file the IR4 return while carrying on a taxable business in New Zealand, or falsifying records to conceal New Zealand-source income from Ro-Ro freight or charter hire. Also includes using a Cook Islands IC as a conduit to avoid tax while actual management is in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 for evasion or defeating tax may result in a fine of up to NZ$50,000 for a first offence and NZ$100,000 for subsequent offences, plus up to 3 years' imprisonment. Civil shortfall penalties range from 20% to 150% of the tax shortfall, with a 150% penalty for evasion or fraudulent intent. Use-of-money interest is payable on all unpaid tax from the due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual directors who knowingly participate in evasion may be personally prosecuted under section 143B, facing fines and imprisonment of up to 3 years. The corporate veil may be pierced if the IC is a sham or used for fraud, and directors may be personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. The IRD may issue a director penalty notice for unpaid PAYE or GST only if the company is a resident employer, but for other taxes directors may be liable under the Companies Act 1993 for reckless trading or under the sham doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the Cook Islands IC solely to hold the shares of the vessel-owning company or to issue invoices for charter hire while the actual employees, operations, bank accounts, and management decisions are located in New Zealand. No physical office, staff, or operational oversight in the Cook Islands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IC will be deemed a New Zealand tax resident under the CMC test, exposing its worldwide income to 28% corporate tax. General anti-avoidance provisions may recharacterise the entire arrangement, voiding tax benefits, and shortfall penalties up to 40% or 150% may apply. The IC may also be struck off by the Cook Islands Registrar for failure to maintain substance requirements, and its registered agent may be penalised. New Zealand courts may impose penalties for failure to disclose foreign entity interests under the foreign trust disclosure regime, if applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are New Zealand residents and exercise effective control over the IC may be personally assessed as directors of a deemed New Zealand resident company. The IRD may pierce the veil where the IC is a mere facade; directors may be personally liable for fines, and travel bans may be imposed to compel compliance. Under the Companies Act 1993, directors may be liable for obligations incurred while trading while insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence on charterers or beneficial owners, concealing the identity of persons with ultimate control of the Ro-Ro shipping operations, or processing Swift LC and wire transfer payments through the IC without adequate AML controls. Also includes handling payments from sanctioned entities or jurisdictions using the IC to circumvent international sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: New Zealand's Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 applies to financial institutions, but a non-resident IC is not a reporting entity unless it is a financial service provider. However, New Zealand trustees, registered agents, or accountants providing services may be reporting entities. Breaches of AML laws can attract civil penalties up to NZ$2 million for companies and NZ$200,000 for individuals per contravention. Sanctions violations under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and other autonomous sanctions can result in fines up to NZ$250,000 and imprisonment of up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of reporting entities can be personally liable for fines and imprisonment for serious non-compliance. If the IC is used for money laundering, individuals can be prosecuted under the Crimes Act 1961, with imprisonment of up to 14 years. Directors may also be subject to asset freezing and extradition in relation to cross-border financial crime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in related-party cross-border transactions (e.g., charter hire paid to an associated foreign vessel-owning company) exceeding NZ$10 million without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or using a non-arm's-length pricing structure that strips profit out of New Zealand without an OECD-aligned analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD may adjust taxable income to the arm's-length amount, impose shortfall penalties of 20% (without reasonable care) or 40% (with manipulation), and apply UOMI. If the failure is found to be fraudulent, a 150% penalty may apply. The taxpayer bears the burden of proving that the pricing was arm's-length; failure to produce documentation will likely result in an unfavourable reconstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the tax return knowing that transfer pricing positions are indefensible may be personally liable for penalties for false statements. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, directors who are knowingly party to preparing incorrect tax returns may be prosecuted and imprisoned for up to 3 years. In a sham scenario, directors may be personally liable for the entire tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Trust and Disclosure Non-Compliance (if applicable)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: If the IC is owned by a New Zealand foreign trust, failing to register the trust with the IRD, failing to file the annual foreign trust disclosure return (IR634), or failing to report settlements and distributions. Non-resident settlors who are New Zealand residents are taxed on worldwide income from the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: New Zealand foreign trusts are subject to registration and annual disclosure requirements. Failure to comply attracts penalties of NZ$1,000 for each annual return not filed. If the trust is deemed resident and the IC's income is attributed to the settlor, income tax at 28% plus penalties and interest apply. The IRD can also assess the trustee as a representative for the settlor's unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Trustees (often directors of ICs) are personally liable for trust penalties and for taxes assessed on the trust if they fail to comply. New Zealand resident settlors who fail to disclose offshore ICs may be criminally liable for evasion. Individuals may be subject to travel bans and criminal sanctions for concealing offshore assets.
